key_insight: The paper shows that spin-qubit quantum computers can become energetically competitive with classical computing before they achieve an execution-time advantage, especially when energy is measured for QFT workloads and then extended to fault-tolerant operation.
engineering_relevance: For scalable quantum hardware design, the dominant constraints are cryogenic cooling, control electronics, and decoding overheads, making energy-efficient system architecture as important as qubit performance.
method: Built a detailed energy budget for a Loss-DiVincenzo spin-qubit computer running the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT).
Benchmarked QFT energy use against the classical Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) under polynomially bounded sampling assumptions.
Extended the analysis to surface-code QEC, including QEC cycles, gate synthesis, decoding, and control-signal demultiplexing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that optimized demultiplexing can cut total energy by roughly two orders of magnitude and estimates about 100 kW power for a system with around one million physical qubits.
watch_item: The power estimates depend strongly on cryogenic and control-stack assumptions, so real hardware implementations may shift the crossover points and total energy cost.
paper_title: Energetics of Fault-Tolerant Spin-Qubit Quantum Computation
